new_statements.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
new_statements.rule_in_words: No Ai-Cham-specific rule is stated anywhere accessible. The only opened statement is a family-level survey line: Tai-Kadai languages (Ai-Cham listed under Kam-Sui) are tonal with monosyllabic morphemes; the survey gives no word-accent information for any Kam-Sui language. Primary descriptions (Lin & Cui 1988; Yang 2000; Cui 1999) could not be opened; Google Books snippet probes of Lin & Cui 1988 find tones (nine tones in Diwo/Gengfang per Chinese sources) but no occurrence of 'stress'.
new_statements.exceptions: None for Ai-Cham; the survey's only accentual remarks in this section concern Thai and Lao (final stress in polysyllabic words/compounds).
new_statements.domain_note: Family-level generalisation about Tai-Kadai as a whole, not a description of Ai-Cham; second-hand and not tied to a cited Ai-Cham source.
new_statements.identity_note: Ai-Cham [aih] = Chinese 锦语/锦话 (Jinhua), also 甲姆话 (Jiamuhua), autonym ʔai33 cam11; spoken in Di'e/Diwo 地莪 and Boyao 播尧 townships, Libo county. Lin & Cui 1988 describe two local varieties, Diwo (main) and Boyao (separate sound system). Yang Tongyin 2000 treats Ai-Cham as the 锦 dialect of Mo/Mak [mkg] (Glottolog: the book 'mostly draws on Ai-Cham which is considered a sister dialect'), so any stress statement in Yang 2000 must be checked for which dialect it covers. The survey line quoted is about the Tai-Kadai family as a whole.
